newsitem.title: UK: Euro Products Outlook - Gasoline strong, fuel weak.
newsitem.headline: Euro Products Outlook - Gasoline strong, fuel weak.

text.p: While Europe's oil products will be supported this week by refiners' perceptions their output is too cheap when compared to crude, middle distillates and fuel oil are well supplied and are currently unattractive to buyers.

Gasoline is moving into a higher gear -- strong interest from the United States as the summer driving starts in earnest, cuts in refinery crude throughputs announced last week in Europe, and hoarding ahead of an anticipated duty hike in the post-election British budget.
"I don't see anything on the horizon which will send them lower," one trader said.
Eurograde barges were worth $211 a tonne fob ARA on Monday though holidays in the U.K. and the U.S. killed most trade.

But British newspapers said their new government's first budget, which may include a tax increase on gasoline and has already led to hoarding by some traders, may be delayed from June 10 to June 25 or July 2. This would lead to some prompt selling and an easing in the price backwardation, traders said.

Monday's Memorial Day holiday in the U.S. traditionally marks the beginning of the driving season, and traders reckon 150-200,000 tonnes of gasoline have already been sold across the Atlantic between May 15 and June 5. More may follow, they say.
Naphtha was expected to remain weak for prompt delivery, with many buyers holding out for higher prices into June.
Gas oil may weaken, because buying in the key German market is poor. Heating oil barge premiums to June IPE shed $1 to $2 a tonne last week, but demand was still slack on Monday.
"We're ready for a dip," said one trader in Rotterdam.
Diesel premiums were also expected to slip below June IPE +$10 with supplies moving in from the Med, where Russian and Italian barrels are sailing into an already-long market.

Differentials to benchmark Med quotes shed around $2.50 last week as very prompt and distressed cargoes scrambled for homes. Traders said prices were unlikely to recover from the high cif quotes -$1.50 a tonne basis Genoa.

High sulphur fuel barges have bumped along in the $80-$85 a tonne fob range for some two months and weak numbers look set to continue with the start-up in earnest of the summer export programme from St. Petersburg.
Unusually, much of the Russian fuel has been cracked material, rather than the anticipated straight-run which is quite rare and commanding healthy premiums.
Traders are holding their breath for a fall.
"The market is more bearish than bullish," said one. "We'll bump up and down for a while then it'll crash below $70 (fob ARA), I think."

Low sulphur cargoes jumped by $5 last week on the back of a single deal. But there have been no other physical trades seen since, no cargoes are thought due until June and numbers are largely dictated by the swaps market.

Med fuel markets are also becoming saturated with Russian material, with both bunker and refinery buyers relaxed and prices under pressure to head to levels below even where they were before crude began its recent rise.
